summary: One project is counted as playable by its own report, and nobody else has checked it. Vice-Tay's documents describe one session of 30 minutes in the world, played by hand through a scripted gamepad, at a median of 21.1 frames a second on an RTX 4090 on the smaller console's profile; this page read it at 20:47 UTC and 21:22 UTC on 26 November. The first 4 minutes are cutscenes, the picture has faults and its README sets a goal of 30 and lists the frame time among its known problems. PortWatch calls Belobug's build very playable at about 22 on average with no crashes, with no session length, and VIctory-RDNA reports a capture of under ten minutes at medians of 19.1 to 23.1 at 4K output. klbf-lab's newest test build reports 37 minutes so far of play in the open world on a Radeon RX 9070 XT at 14.0 frames a second on average. VIctory-7900XTX reports a city street at about 22 with renderer patches that are off by default. Press reports of 26 November relay posts and videos that claim 25 to 30 for builds of CGBJ's code, and one says a packaged build is circulating; none gives a session length and none is verified. PortWatch still relays 25 for CGBJ itself, which it lists as a private build again since its repository stopped answering that morning, and outside runs of its published code measured 2.7 on its own settings and, with settings changed on an RTX 3080, 19.6 and later about 22 to 25. Playable needs 20 for 30 minutes in one session of play, reported as such.

forecast.definition: At least one project reports the game in-game and under player control for 30 minutes or more without a crash, at 20 frames per second or better on some PC, counting rendered frames only.
basis: What was reported: one session on Vice-Tay's own test PC, an RTX 4090 with a Ryzen 9 9950X3D, on the smaller console's profile: 30 minutes in the world, played by hand from the prison through a boat section to an island on foot, at a median of 21.1 frames a second, with 19.1 to 23.2 for the middle 80 percent and a 1% low of 17.0.

Where it comes from: the project's README, test page and measurements page, read by this page at 20:47 UTC and 21:22 UTC on 26 November. The frame rate is taken from the game's own frame lines, so the frames are rendered and none are generated. Read again at 04:44 UTC on 27 November, after the README was rewritten, with the test and measurements pages unchanged on the session.

What nobody has checked: all of it. No outside tester and no second machine has reproduced the session, and this page reads documents and runs nothing. A contributor's notes in its repository give eight exploratory samples on an RTX 4070 on the larger console's profile, at a mean frame time of 76.6 milliseconds, about 13 frames a second, and short samples on an RTX 5070 Ti on the smaller one, at 17.6 to 21.6 frames a second over 14 to 56 seconds, which are not a second run of the session.

What the report itself qualifies: by hand means pad inputs sent through a script while watching a capture after every move, the first 4 of the 30 minutes are cutscenes, three failed attempts were picked up at checkpoints, and the current documents give the session's length and timeline without saying in words how it ended, which an earlier README did by saying the test runner ended it.

What it is not: the console's experience. The README, rewritten on 27 November, lists colour banding, flat-colour surfaces, blocky clouds and reflections and missing or incorrect shading, puts the frame time among its known problems against its own goal of 30 frames a second, and reports only the opening stretch of the game on a top graphics card.

What could undo it: the project withdrawing or correcting the report, an outside run that contradicts it, or the repository going away. GitHub's published notice of 24 November against Leonida is still the only one that names a listed project.

projects.status: Its README (18:57 UTC on 27 November) says the world loads and gives player control, saved games load, and sunlight, shadows, room lighting and screen reflections are right, and reports 3.1 to 3.4 frames a second at the prison checkpoint, 3.0 at 1080p output, and 2.0 driving the boat, the median of a 9-minute play run at 1080p output, on a MacBook Pro M4 Pro with 48 GB, on the larger console's profile. It says the boat's 4.8 to 4.9 frames a second (4.9 at 1080p), and the earlier 4.7 and 6.0, were the cutscene that opens the boat mission and not driving, lists objects that flicker black for a frame, a controller that stopped responding soon after driving began in one play run, night streets and rooms flatter than on the console, one black patch on water and distant trees and buildings that appear 5 to 35 seconds late after a camera cut, says playable speed is not reached with a next goal of 5 and then 10 at 1080p, and relays ten other Macs' reports, from 0.2 to 4.1 frames a second, which this page does not read into a lane.

picture.text: sun, shadows and room light right; black flicker and patches

speed.text: 2.0 fps driving the boat, 3.1 to 3.4 at the prison checkpoint

projects.name: DanziLoader-Cpp
projects.kind: C++20 port of a runtime in the VIctory line
projects.status: Its maintainer's results files, on a separate branch of its repository (04:50 UTC on 27 November), report a player with a controller going from the boat section to a section on foot and then to flight in one 30-minute session that was still running at the end, at 6.05 frames a second by two counters, on an RTX 5080 on the smaller console's profile at half render scale, with 17.5 in a cutscene on a later build and 7 to 8.3 in two 60-second boat samples. It says the figures do not show a sustained 20 and that water and lighting faults and uneven frame pacing remain, and its main README (21:11 UTC on 26 November) still reports a session of more than 16 minutes and about 11 in a 45-second sample; nobody else has confirmed any of it.

picture.text: water and lighting faults named; shading not described

speed.text: 6.05 fps average over 30 minutes at half render scale

stability.text: 30 minutes by hand, still running when it ended

projects.name: M1LK
projects.kind: Fork of VIctory and the DexNom fork for NVIDIA cards with 8 GB, published on 26 November
projects.status: Its README (14:59 UTC on 27 November) says the player controls the character in the opening scenes, with walking, sprinting, strafing, jumping, mouse look and the pause menu responding, and reports a walking median of 4.5 frames a second, with lows of 3.6, on an RTX 4060 Laptop with 8 GB on the smaller console's profile with ray tracing off, from scripted keyboard and mouse runs. It says the picture is complete but dark without ray tracing, with interiors and backlit people near black, that no crash appears in its logs of tests 14 to 35 while the longest session without one is 20 minutes and a 40-minute run is not done, and that the processor side limits speed; nobody else has confirmed any of it.

picture.text: outdoor and window light lit; interiors near black

speed.text: 4.5 fps walking median in the latest scripted runs

stability.text: 20 minutes, no crash; 40-minute run not done yet

projects.basis: Project README: the maintainer's own figures from one laptop, from scripted keyboard and mouse runs; not confirmed by anyone else

projects.name: VIctorious
projects.kind: Fork of VIctory by way of VIctory-7900XTX, tuned for AMD RDNA 4 cards
projects.status: Its README on the 7900-base branch (16:13 UTC on 27 November) reports a title it does not name running with the player driving in the world on an RX 9070 XT with a Ryzen 7 9800X3D and 32 GB of RAM on the smaller console's profile, at about 38 milliseconds a frame, 26 frames a second, with lamps that can flicker and trees that can pop, or about 43, 23 frames a second, with stable lights, in scenes of 4,000 to 7,000 draws a frame, and at 15 to 17 frames a second on the larger console's profile, which it calls sharper and heavier. It lists a little geometry flicker, textures of roads and buildings that can be late or black while the game streams and frame generation that flickers at today's real frame rate, reports no run length or crash status for this fork, and sets a goal of a steady 30 frames a second that it says it has not reached; nobody else has confirmed any of it.

picture.text: lit; lamps flicker, trees pop, road textures late or black

speed.text: about 23 to 26 fps driving, smaller console's profile

stability.text: no run length reported

projects.name: PercyScarlett
projects.kind: Xbox Series compatibility layer, with a runtime now built on VIctory and victory-fork
projects.basis: Project README and its guide, measured on one machine
projects.status: Its v1.0, whose runtime is now built on VIctory, victory-fork and ScarlettPort, reaches the opening scene of a title it does not name, lit and textured, at about 2 to 3 frames a second on an RTX 2060 SUPER at reduced resolution. It says speed is far from playable and shaded areas are too dark, and it reports nothing about control in the scene.

projects.name: Scarlight
projects.kind: Steam compatibility tool for Linux based on VIctory and victory-fork, through Mesa's open-source drivers
projects.status: Its README, rewritten on 25 November as a Steam compatibility tool for Linux, reports a title it does not name with its world shown only partly, lit and textured in places and dark in much of the scene, at 1.5 to 3 frames a second in a fixed test scene and as little as 0.1 in busy ones on a Radeon RX 9070 XT. It says menus, sound and the controller work, some builds hang at start or when the world loads, and it is not playable.
projects.basis: Project README, measured on a fixed test scene

projects.name: XCL
projects.kind: Compatibility layer for Xbox Series games
projects.basis: Project README and its commit notes. The run into the world is on a branch that is not merged
projects.status: Its README says that with a branch not yet merged, the newer retail game it does not name goes on from its menus into its 3D world at about 5 frames a second on an RTX 5090, and it has withdrawn an earlier figure of 14 that averaged in the menus and loading. It says the game is not playable: the picture of the world is incomplete and it does not keep running there for long, and it does not say whether the player has control.

projects.name: VIctory-macOS
projects.kind: Runs VIctory on Apple Silicon Macs through CrossOver Wine and Apple's D3DMetal
projects.basis: Project README, from testers' reports on several Macs
projects.status: Tester reports in its README (05:58 UTC on 27 November) say an M2 Pro reached the prologue's first gameplay prompt, where the camera followed input at about 2 seconds a world frame, with one run lasting almost 35 minutes before the game's watchdog stopped it, an M1 Max reached the world and the opening credits at 0.4 to 3.4 seconds a world frame with a warm shader cache, and a change now on by default took a world frame from 2.9 seconds to 0.88 on an M4 and from 5.29 to 0.71 on an M4 Pro, with lighting still broken. Its summary still says nobody has reached gameplay and that the game is not playable on a Mac or anywhere else.

projects.name: five-star-recomp
projects.kind: GTA VI recompilation toolchain
projects.basis: Project status page
projects.status: Shows every first-run screen, loads story mode and runs the opening scenes, with a world frame taking about 200 to 400 milliseconds. Its status page (20:28 UTC on 27 November) says geometry, normals and depth are right, that sun with cascade shadows, a sky and a stand-in ambient term now reach the frame, so that the first scene's yard reads as the game's sunset scene, with bars of sunlight where there should be shadow, dark lamps and some black blocks still wrong, that a translator fix for literal samplers has cleared the posterized rings and most of the smear after post-processing, that the picture no longer freezes on a white card because a translator bug that let a shadow program overwrite the start of a graphics heap is fixed, so the game shows its first scene as live 3D, and that the NVIDIA device loss is fixed in one 14-minute boot, with an RTX 5090 report still losing the device earlier in another way.

projects.name: Leonida Continued
projects.kind: Continuation of Leonida, the halted GTA VI recompilation
projects.basis: Project README and its Linux test report: the world frames are from one Linux machine with a Radeon RX 7900 XTX, and the earlier results from about 80 starts on a Linux machine and runs on a Windows machine
projects.status: Its Linux report of 26 November says one machine with a Radeon RX 7900 XTX drew the project's first frames of the world, a street at night and one at sunset with palm trees, cars and a character, during eight minutes in the world with no GPU hang, at roughly one frame every six seconds. Its README, last changed at 02:49 UTC, still says no frame of the world has been verified on any test machine and that nothing is playable, and nothing reports control in the world.

projects.name: OpenScarlett (Community Edition)
projects.kind: Compatibility layer for Xbox Series games, separate from the other OpenScarlett
projects.basis: Project README, tested on one machine
projects.status: Runs a newer retail game it does not name through its first-boot settings and legal screens, start screen and 4K intro video with sound, at a steady 30 frames a second. It stops while the scene behind the menus streams in.

projects.name: Xbox2Windows
projects.kind: Translation toolchain for Xbox Series games
projects.basis: Project README
projects.status: With a modified diagnostic copy of the executable and a debugger set to continue past assertions, a run on an RTX 4060 laptop played the intro video, got through setup and reached loading. The project says start-up of the original executable is unverified, and it does not name the title.

projects.name: OpenScarlett
projects.kind: Compatibility layer for Xbox Series games
projects.basis: Commit messages, tested on one machine
projects.status: Its README (05:20 UTC) reports a retail title it does not name running through its 4K intro video, first-run and legal menus and loading screens at 30 to 60 frames a second on a 4 GB GTX 1650 Ti, with more than 6 GiB of game data streamed in. It names the step from loading into live 3D gameplay as what comes next.

projects.name: TuxBox
projects.kind: Compatibility layer for Linux (Proton)
projects.basis: Project README, progress page and run records from two machines
projects.status: Its documents (12:45 UTC) now say the game reaches the prologue cutscene, which appears, and then crashes, that it is not playable and that 4,411 of 41,064 captured shader requests are still unsupported. Its longest recorded run, an earlier one on Linux, got into the story intro by the game's own state and lasted 18 minutes 11 seconds, with the graphics queues stalling, before ending on a game assert.

projects.name: Port of the Americas
projects.kind: Compatibility layer for Linux (Proton), for GTA VI only
projects.basis: Project README, tested on one machine
projects.status: Its README reports the press-start screen, the first-time setup pages and loading-screen artwork drawing on Linux under Proton on a Radeon RX 9070 XT, with a button press starting the boot flow. It says the world load runs without a crash but the world draws black.

projects.name: keylime
projects.kind: Runtime written from scratch in C++, drawing through Vulkan
projects.basis: Project README: the maintainer's own claims, with no test machine named and no outside report
projects.status: Its repository stopped answering over git between 22:28 and 22:59 UTC on 25 November, with no published takedown notice naming it and the reason not known. Its README last said the game boots natively and shows its intro, main menu and loading screen at 30 frames a second with sound, with gameplay not reached.

projects.name: GTA6-BootTest
projects.kind: GTA VI boot harness with its own shader translator
projects.basis: Project README
projects.status: Boots the game, runs its frame loop and draws its first interface screen, the start-screen prompt bar, through translated shaders. Compute shaders, tiled textures and blending are unfinished.

projects.name: g6shim
projects.kind: Replacement system libraries for Xbox console games
projects.basis: Project README
projects.status: Renders at about 12 frames a second up to the account picker of a Series title it identifies only by number. Its next goals are an offline user and the main menu.

projects.name: Holy-Interoperability
projects.kind: Compatibility layer for Xbox Series games
projects.basis: Project README
projects.status: Shows the first screen of a retail title it does not name, an account prompt with its text drawn correctly and a background that covers only half the screen, at a steady 30 frames a second after frames that were black. Its README (20:29 UTC on 27 November) says the title ran for 90 seconds, the longest it has tested so far, with the host's graphics debug layer finding nothing, that it waits at the prompt because nobody is signed in, that the device removals of its earlier runs came from a buffer view reaching past its buffer, which it now keeps inside, and that no title is playable yet.

projects.name: Leonida
projects.kind: GTA VI recompilation, halted
projects.basis: GitHub's published takedown notices, press reports of the creator's public posts, and git checks from this page
projects.status: Halted since 23 November, when its creator stepped away, saying Rockstar had the project's Discord server taken down and, PC Gamer reports, sharing the notice Discord sent. On 24 November GitHub published a Take-Two takedown notice against its repository and applied it to all 3,007 repositories in its fork network.

projects.name: palmetto
projects.kind: Compatibility runtime for a console build, by one maintainer
projects.basis: Project README and commit notes, and git checks from this page
projects.status: Its README reports the title booting, executing its draws and presenting frames in its own window, with the picture still black. Its commit notes say the repository descends from the project network that received Take-Two's notice, and that it removed the game's and that project's names in response.

projects.name: xbox-emulator
projects.kind: Compatibility layer for Xbox Series games
projects.basis: Second-hand, from a community project list
projects.status: A contributor's notes reportedly reach the game window and graphics device. The repository has had no commits since 11:58 UTC.

watching.name: Palmwave
watching.note: Was a fork of XCL, then from 21:12 UTC on 24 November a renamed copy of victory-fork with a few commits of its own. Its repository stopped answering at about 22:15 UTC, with no published takedown notice naming it and the reason not known. The same account published Kelvaroq on 25 November, which is in the table.

watching.name: project-flamingo
watching.note: A fork of VIctory with its own pull-request queue, which Scarlight's README points NVIDIA and Windows users to. Its README still carries VIctory's status from 23 November and reports no results of its own.

watching.name: G6Recomp
watching.note: Now creates the game's window, graphics device, command queues and lists, with memory code ported from Leonida. No frame yet.

watching.name: XValkyrie
watching.note: Runs other Xbox Series games and has published work on a later title's first frames, without naming it. It bundled a copy of the VIctory engine for about 20 minutes on 24 November, removed it, and now ports parts of VIctory's texture code with credit.

watching.name: ScarlettX
watching.note: No GTA VI work published.

watching.name: scarlett-layer
watching.note: No GTA VI work published.

watching.name: AnyPS5
watching.note: The PlayStation route: it relinks PS5 executables to run on Linux and Windows. Press reports of 25 and 26 November say a PS5 build of the game has leaked and was shown running on a jailbroken console, unverified; nothing in its repository names this title so far.

watching.name: XSXEmu
watching.note: A Rust emulator for Xbox Series titles on Apple Silicon that does not use Wine. Its README now says the game's own code starts under Rosetta and opens its archives, and that it has not yet created a graphics device, run a shader or produced a frame.

watching.name: Xenstride
watching.note: Its v0.3.0 runtime is now based on VIctory, where earlier versions derived from XCL, with its own changes to texture staging, readback, descriptor views and shader rounding. Its status page says commercial titles, gameplay and in-game performance remain unverified: its measurements are of a synthetic scene of its own.

watching.name: gta-vi-astral
watching.note: A system written in Go and documented in French. Its README now says the intro screens' interface draws on a graphics card at 30 frames a second in runs of 65 seconds without a crash, with navigable menus in progress and no 3D picture or sound yet, and calls it not playable.

watching.name: victory-world-runtime
watching.note: A fork of VIctory that gathers fixes from the public forks, and the base DexNom RayTime builds on. Its README still carries victory-fork's earlier status and reports no results of its own.

watching.name: VIctory-forkAMD
watching.note: A fork of VIctory on victory-fork's line for one modest AMD PC, a Radeon RX 7600 with 8 GB. Its README (15:04 UTC on 26 November, in French) reports 8.9 frames a second on average over a 15-minute walk in the opening prison on the larger console's profile with upscaling, without a crash and with walls sometimes missing, and 6.1 to 6.8 on a later build with the walls present, which it calls its valid reference. Its notes on the code PortWatch lists as CGBJ, read but not run, put that code's own documents at 13 to 22 frames a second and call the 25 relayed for it exaggerated; nobody has verified either.

watching.name: HybridGt
watching.note: Engineering work built on another project's runtime, tested on an RTX 4070 Ti, which since its 0.2.0 release is VIctory-NVIDIA's with its own patches on top, where it ran inside victory-fork before. Its README (13:43 UTC on 27 November) reports a median of 14.2 frames a second in the world, best 18.0, against 5.8 for its earlier runtime over the same scripted route, with 5.6 GB of graphics memory in use against 9.2. Its performance notes still list textures that look pixelated or off-colour until they load and eyes and mouths that look wrong, and relay a tester's remark of a stable 15 frames a second, which this page does not count.

watching.name: Sixth Star
watching.note: A compatibility layer built from VIctory's code and tested on an RTX 3070 with 8 GB. Its status file (00:39 UTC on 27 November) reports gameplay at about 0.7 frames a second, a median over one run of about 5 minutes on a newer build, slower than the 4.6 it measured on 26 November on an earlier build, and says a later change is not measured on the title yet; a 33-minute stability run ended by itself after about 6 minutes, which its maintainer saw as a crash.

watching.name: ScarlettCompat
watching.note: A compatibility layer written from scratch in C++. Its README says the game's executable loads and runs as far as creating graphics pipelines, with no game frame and no menu yet.

watching.name: victory-nvidia-8gb
watching.note: A fork of victory-fork for NVIDIA cards with 8 GB, and the base Vertex builds on. Its README reports 8 to 10 frames a second on a laptop RTX 4060 with 8 GB and states no session length.

watching.name: CCS03
watching.note: A fork of victory-fork for NVIDIA cards with 8 GB, tested on a laptop RTX 4060. Its README reports play under control at 3 to 7.8 frames a second through the opening and onto the water, in runs of up to 31 minutes without a crash.

watching.name: VKarameloVI
watching.note: VIctory-NVIDIA as set up and measured on a second machine, an RTX 4060 Ti with a Ryzen 5 5600X. Its README reports about 7 to 12 frames a second in the world on the smaller console's profile at half render scale. Its repository stopped answering between 11:22 and 11:44 UTC on 26 November: missing, private or removed, with no published takedown notice naming it and the reason not known.

watching.name: XTP
watching.note: A compatibility layer for Xbox Series titles on Windows, tested on a Radeon RX 6700 XT. Its README says no title is usable yet: menus draw, and in the world most of the scene is missing and frames take seconds. klbf-lab credits it for a fix.

watching.name: ShakiraRED(dt)
watching.note: A performance fork of VIctory's code, credited by AnyXboxX and tested on an RTX 4090 on the larger console's profile. Its README gives single samples from gameplay scenes, not averages: 18 to 20 frames a second in a lighter scene, 13.7 to 15 in a heavier one and 1.8 in a spike, with some draws dropped for missing pipelines and no session length. It does not name its title and has had no commits since 25 November.

watching.name: Native VIctory for macOS
watching.note: A port of VIctory to macOS that uses no Wine: the game's code runs in its own process and its graphics go straight to Metal. Its README says the game boots on a Mac, gets past its start screen and runs for about 50 seconds, with menus drawn to an internal target while the window is still black. It says it is not playable yet.

watching.name: Neptune + GDeflate
watching.note: A source-only tree of the Neptune edition of VIctory, the edition klbf-lab's newest test build is based on and AnyXboxX used until 26 November, with a faster loading path for the game's packed files and upscaling through a third-party tool. Its README last gave build notes and no measurements of its own and offered frame generation as an option, and generated frames never count here. Its repository stopped answering by 18:59 UTC on 27 November, with no published takedown notice naming it and the reason not known.

watching.name: VIctory-reloaded
watching.note: A fork of VIctory that builds on victory-fork, aimed at NVIDIA cards and tested on an RTX 4090 on the larger console's profile. Its README reports about 6 frames a second in the world, limited by the processor side of its graphics emulation, the first gameplay shot rendering like the console with ray tracing still off, and no crash in its test runs. It says it is not playable yet.

watching.name: Kitty6
watching.note: A fork of VIctory-7900XTX for an RTX 4070 with 12 GB, added at its maintainer's request in this page's issues. Its README of 26 November reports a median of 20.5 frames a second standing in the opening scene on the smaller console's profile and 24 to 28 in scripted walking with dips to 13, in runs of about 5 minutes, and says that none is a played session yet and that it is not playable yet.

watching.name: ApexVI
watching.note: A fork of VIctory tuned for a laptop RTX 4050 with 6 GB, added at its maintainer's request in this page's issues. Its README reports a controllable character at 6.35 to 7.5 frames a second by scene and runs of 14 to 15 minutes without a crash. Its maintainer has renamed the repository from ApexIV to ApexVI.

watching.name: VIcky
watching.note: A research fork that builds on victory-fork for NVIDIA cards, credited by ScarlettPort. Its README reports about 6.2 frames a second on an RTX 4080 on the larger console's profile with the title's own ray tracing on, from three runs, with a dark quarter of the picture in some rooms.

watching.name: VIctory Polaris build
watching.note: A build of VIctory for older Radeon cards without mesh shaders, tested on an RX 500-series card with 8 GB. Its README says it is not playable: menus, map, sound and 2D screens work, and the 3D world is still black at about 1 frame a second or worse.

watching.name: playablegames-peppa
watching.note: A fork of VIctory that carries victory-fork's and VIctory-7900XTX's work, aimed at NVIDIA cards and tested on an RTX 5080 with a Ryzen 7 5700X3D on the smaller console's profile with the title's own upscaler at two-thirds scale and ray tracing off. Its README says a 55-minute session played with a controller ended without a crash and reports 23.5 frames a second over 12 minutes (22.8 to 23.9 over three 5-minute runs) with the character standing in a house interior and a button pressed every 10 seconds, so it gives no frame rate from play; it does not name its title and its goal is 30.

watching.name: Victory Grimkaaah
watching.note: A build of VIctory for AMD Radeon cards only, tested on an RX 7900 XTX with a Ryzen 9 7950X3D on the larger console's profile. Its README (version 1.0 of 27 November) reports 24.3 frames a second on average in busy world scenes with ray tracing off and 13.9 with it on, over sessions of 3 to 9 minutes with no crash or card loss in its last 10 sessions; it does not name its title or say whether the player was in control.

watching.name: Tequesta
watching.note: A Rust compatibility layer and Direct3D 12 translation runtime for NVIDIA RTX cards on Windows, with its own settings overlay and native keyboard and mouse input, tested on an RTX A4500 with 28 GB of system memory. Its README (11:06 UTC) reports player control and camera movement in the game's prison section and about 8 to 9 frames a second on average at 1080p, with 2 to 14 in active 3D scenes, down from the 5 to 27 it listed earlier today. It gives no session length and no crash record, and it lists lighting and shadows as partial, static faces in cutscenes and skin artifacts.

watching.name: victory-rtx3060
watching.note: A fork of VIctory-NVIDIA for an RTX 3060 12 GB with a Ryzen 5 5600X, with measurements from 26 November. Its README headlines 14 to 17 frames a second in the open world after warming up, from scripted 6-minute runs averaging 13.6 to 15.0 with the character standing in one place, plus a 17-minute open-world stretch at 12 to 14 that it does not describe as played. It reports no session of play with a length, so it stays on the watch list.

watching.name: VIctory-AMD-4K
watching.note: A fork of VIctory for AMD RDNA2 cards with 16 GB of system memory, tested on a Radeon RX 6800 with a Ryzen 5 5600 at native 4K with ray tracing off. Its README reports full 3D gameplay with a gamepad and a mouse camera at 13.0 to 16.1 frames a second, with no graphics device timeouts across sessions of 10 minutes or more, from one PC. It gives no session length or average, so it stays here until a played session with one is reported.

watching.name: El1xr
watching.note: A fork of AnyXboxX that, by its README (19:16 UTC on 27 November), calls the game playable in the open world, with a median of 23.5 frames a second in the world at 4K on an RTX 5090, read from the in-world part of one quiet 200-second test run that starts from a fixed checkpoint. Its older figures, from an RTX 4070 SUPER, are about 4 frames a second over a 13-minute session and a reported 2 over 45 minutes, and it lists black or blotched faces in about half of test runs and a stall of 3 to 9 seconds on entering the world. It stays here until a played session of 10 minutes or more with an average on its current build is reported.

updates.title: Holy-Interoperability's title now shows its first screen
points: Holy-Interoperability, a compatibility layer for Xbox Series games, says in its README (20:29 UTC on 27 November) that a retail title it does not name now shows its first screen, an account prompt with its text drawn correctly and a background that covers half the screen, where its frames had been black.

It reports the title running at a steady 30 frames a second for the 90 seconds it has tested so far, with no error from the host's graphics debug layer, and waiting at the prompt because nobody is signed in; it says no title is playable yet and puts its overall progress at about 33 percent, from 27.
That moves it from first frames to a recognisable picture, level with GTA6-BootTest and g6shim, which also reach only a first interface screen. The report is the project's own and unconfirmed.

updates.title: victory-fork's newest figures put its speed lane at 10 to 12.6 frames a second
points: victory-fork says in its README (20:14 UTC on 27 November) that, with a new memory gate that keeps the card under its budget, one play session on an RTX 4070 at 1920x1080 with its own ray tracing on ran at about 12.6 frames a second at 5,000 to 7,000 draws a frame and about 10 at 7,000 to 12,000, where it had said about 15 and about 8 for other bands of draws.
Its speed lane now reads 10 to 12.6, still the fourth step, and its place and every other lane are unchanged. The figures are the maintainer's own, from one PC, and unconfirmed.

updates.title: PortWatch now says GitHub removed VIctory-7900XTX over its Terms of Service
points: PortWatch, which listed VIctory-7900XTX as offline at 18:40 UTC on 27 November and said it was not known whether GitHub or its owner removed it, said at 19:38 UTC that GitHub removed the repository and its owner's account for a Terms of Service violation, as it says of VIctory-Belobug-AMD, and that it confirmed this.

GitHub publishes no notice of removals under its Terms of Service, so nothing here can check that; the repository still does not answer over git, and GitHub's public notice log, whose newest entry is from 25 November, names neither it nor VIctory-Belobug-AMD.
The row keeps the figures it last reported, from a README read before the repository stopped answering, and carries no link.

updates.title: El1xr joins the watch list with a median of 23.5 frames a second from a short test run
points: El1xr, a fork of AnyXboxX, says in its README (19:16 UTC on 27 November) that the game is playable in the open world, with a median of 23.5 frames a second at 4K on an RTX 5090, read from the in-world part of one quiet 200-second test run that starts from a fixed checkpoint.

That is a test run and not a played session, so it fills no lane and does not meet the bar, which asks for 30 minutes at 20 or more in one session of play. Its older played figures, on an RTX 4070 SUPER, are about 4 frames a second over 13 minutes and a reported 2 over 45 minutes.
The figures are the project's own, from one machine, and unconfirmed. The entry stays under Also watched until a played session of 10 minutes or more with an average on its current build is reported.

updates.title: The Scarlett fork, Vertex and Neptune + GDeflate stop answering
points: None of the three repositories answers over git from here: all three were already failing at 18:59 UTC on 27 November and again at 19:11, 19:39 and 19:44 UTC, while every other linked repository answered.
PortWatch's data does not list any of them, the newest entry in GitHub's public notice log is from 25 November, before they stopped answering, and no reason has been reported.

VIctory-RDNA reports a capture of 9 minutes 38 seconds at a median of 23.1 at 4K output, which would put its speed lane at the bar's step; like any such reading it waits for a second look at the next check. PortWatch now calls Belobug's build very playable at about 22 on average with no crashes, with no session length, while that project's README still reports 5 to 8.

ScarlettPort's rebuilt renderer shows a fuller picture at about 3 frames a second, and it is now 6 steps short. Kitty6 and ApexIV, two projects that asked to be listed, are on the watch list. GitHub has published no new takedown notice, and there is still no statement from Rockstar or Take-Two since the Leonida notice.

updates.title: Automatic checks are paused
points: The last automatic check ran at 16:15 UTC on 26 November. The standings and the estimate on this page are as of that time.
Until updates resume nothing here is re-read: the conditions published with the estimate will not be checked, and Vice-Tay's 30-minute test will not get another reading.
As of that check nothing is counted as playable. Vice-Tay is first with both of its lanes at the bar's steps, on one README sentence about a 30-minute test that its other documents do not yet carry.

updates.title: Victory-United rebuilds on Vice-Tay's code; a tester's Mac reaches the first gameplay prompt
points: Victory-United says it rebuilt its tree on Vice-Tay's code and measured about 11 frames a second standing at a window in the first playable room on an RTX 3080 Ti, at half render scale on the smaller console's profile, in a 7-minute run. That is not play, so its lanes still read the session played by hand on its earlier tree and it stays 10th.

VIctory-macOS: a tester's M2 Pro reached the prologue's first gameplay prompt, where the camera followed input at about 2 seconds a world frame, and one run lasted almost 35 minutes before the game's own watchdog stopped it. The README's summary still says nobody has reached gameplay on a Mac, so it stays at stage 5.

five-star-recomp's status page says its night city now shows only its light sources and that boots since a change of 26 November lose the graphics device before the world. klbf-lab's own five-minute hands-off run on its Radeon RX 9070 XT averaged 14.3 frames a second, which is not play and changes no lane.
Vice-Tay's documents are unchanged at an eighth reading. The estimate was reviewed and held, and the news sweep found no new statement and no new takedown notice.

updates.title: An outside build of CGBJ's code reports a median of 22.4 frames a second on the boat
points: A VIctory contributor's notes (15:33 UTC) say that contributor's own build of the code PortWatch lists as CGBJ now runs at a median of 22.4 frames a second on the boat on an RTX 3080 with 10 GB, on the smaller console's profile, against 18.9 without a fix taken from victory-fork. They say the fix cleared black faces, dark cutscenes, a black sun and colour bands, and that hard-edged rectangles in the water's reflections remain.
The notes give no run length and nobody has verified them, so this stays an outside run: no lane changes, and the estimate does not move on it.
klbf-lab names a newer test build, Lab 63, that it says fixes dark faces in shade. Its figures are still those of the 37-minute session on Lab 61.

updates.title: PortWatch lists CGBJ as a private build again; BRVIctory-ka1qux moves to a faster base
points: PortWatch moved CGBJ back to its private builds at 15:00 UTC, saying its code is offline, and still relays an average of 25 frames a second for it. That is a change of listing and not a withdrawal of its account, so the estimate does not move on it.

At 15:11 UTC PortWatch re-rated pictures: it now rates only DexNom RayTime's as close to the console's and lowered every other build it had rated higher. The picture lanes of the private builds Doomsday and suri, which this page reads from PortWatch, go from step 4 to step 3, and their places are unchanged.

BRVIctory-ka1qux says it rebuilt on VIctory-7900XTX and measures an open-world street at about 10.5 frames a second on a Radeon RX 7800 XT, against 4 to 4.7 before. Those figures are with renderer patches that its launch script leaves off, and it says the snapshot it published has not yet been run in the game, so its lanes still read its earlier base and it stays 23rd.

VIctory-RDNA's two newest captures, about six minutes each and not described as play, end cleanly with medians of 17.2 and 17.9 in their final minute and a peak of 21.9, and its README says a sustained 20 in gameplay remains to be demonstrated. VIctory-macOS reports a tester's M2 Max reaching the opening cinematics in the world at about 2 to 10 seconds a heavy frame.

updates.title: Leonida Continued reports its first frames of the world
points: Its Linux report says one machine with a Radeon RX 7900 XTX drew a street at night and one at sunset with palm trees, cars and a character, during eight minutes in the world with no GPU hang, at roughly one frame every six seconds. It is the first report of the world on screen from the recompilation that continues Leonida.
Its README has not caught up and still says no frame of the world is verified. Nothing reports control, so it stays at stage 5.
The standings and the estimate are unchanged.

updates.title: Vice-Tay is first: a 30-minute test at a median of 21.6 frames a second sets its speed lane; not yet counted as playable
points: Vice-Tay's README still says, at a second reading, that a 30-minute boat test on the smaller console's profile ran at a median of 21.6 frames a second on its RTX 4090, up from 20.5 before a batch of fixes, and calls it a playtest. This page reads a project's speed from its newest session of play, so its speed lane now reads 21.6. With its 70-minute session that puts both of its lanes at the bar's steps, the first row to get there, and it is first, ahead of klbf-lab.

It is not counted as playable. The bar asks for one session that a project reports as played under control for 30 minutes or more without a crash at 20 or better. The README gives this test one sentence, leaves the details to a pull request this page does not read, and still says the build is not fast enough yet; its measurements page and play log do not carry the test. By a fair reading the report may already describe the bar, and the flag changes when the project's own documents say so.

The estimate moves a quarter of a day earlier, to around midnight UTC going into Friday 27 November, with about 5 in 10 by the end of Thursday, on the mark published at 12:22 UTC, met with the caveat above. The new marks are in the revision note.
Kelvaroq's repository has moved to an organisation account, and its row now links there.

updates.title: Vice-Tay reports a median of 21.6 frames a second in a 30-minute boat test; not counted yet
points: Vice-Tay's README (13:22 UTC) says that in a 30-minute boat test on the smaller console's profile, on its RTX 4090, the median frame rate rose from 20.5 to 21.6 frames a second after a batch of fixes. If that was a session of play that ran its 30 minutes, it would be the first report at this page's playable bar.

It is not counted yet. The README gives the claim one sentence and leaves the details to a pull request that it calls a playtest; its measurements page and play log still end with the 70-minute session at 12.9, and nothing in the repository's documents says the test was played under control throughout or ran without a crash. Its own summary still says it is not fast enough yet. Its place, its lanes, the playable flag and the estimate are unchanged, and its documents are re-read at the next check.

VIctory-RDNA moves from the watch list into the table at stage 6, 6th of 31 in-game rows and 1 step short of the bar. Its README (12:54 UTC) now says its maintainer played by hand for about 40 minutes on a Radeon RX 7900 XT at 4K output, at a median of 12.1 frames a second, until the graphics device was removed. Until then the same README said time under player control was unverified for that run, and the row's source line says so.

VIctory-forkAMD, on the watch list, reports 8.9 frames a second on average over a 15-minute walk on a Radeon RX 7600 with 8 GB. PortWatch's automatic scout lists six newly spotted repositories, which are being read.

updates.title: An outside build of CGBJ's code reports about 22 to 25 frames a second on an RTX 3080, with no session length
points: A VIctory contributor's notes (12:47 UTC) now put that contributor's own build of the code PortWatch lists as CGBJ at about 22 to 25 frames a second on an RTX 3080 with 10 GB, on the smaller console's profile with settings of its own, up from a median of 19.6 this morning. The notes call it the set-up that was played and list hard-edged rectangles where a ray-tracing pass is left out, garbled textures on some faces and black skin in some cutscenes. They give no scene and no run length, so it stays an unverified outside run and no lane changes.

Kelvaroq's README says its new memory layer now runs in the open world in a test session, with the work it adds to each frame down from about 6 seconds to between 0.17 and 0.35 seconds against a target of 5 milliseconds. It is not public and comes with no frame rate, so the row's lanes still read its current public build.

On the PlayStation route nothing has changed: the repositories of AnyPS5, AnyKyty and KytyPS5 name this title nowhere. Look-alike repositories that offer a KytyPS5 build for this game as a download now turn up in searches; this page lists none of them, and VGTimes has warned that fake repositories offering builds can carry malware. There is no new takedown notice and no statement from Rockstar or Take-Two.

updates.title: A PlayStation 5 build is reported leaked; nobody has reported running it on a PC
points: Press reports say a PlayStation 5 build of the game has leaked. VGTimes reported a leaker's claim on 25 November, unverified at the time, of a full dump with a decrypted executable. Notebookcheck reported the same day that videos showed a dump of about 540 GB running on a jailbroken console, and calls the footage alleged. This page's earlier news checks did not look for it; a reader pointed it out.

Nobody has reported running that build on a PC. Notebookcheck names the emulator KytyPS5 as a candidate and says considerable work would remain. AnyPS5, the PlayStation route on this page's watch list, has nothing in its repository that names this title, and neither has AnyKyty, a runtime built on AnyPS5 and KytyPS5 that the reader pointed to. Both are read each round.
The reports carry no statement from Rockstar, Take-Two or Sony. The standings and the estimate are unchanged: every listed project works from the Xbox build. This page links to neither leak.

updates.title: VI-BR-PORT, re-read on its new base, reports about 12 frames a second on an 8 GB card; Vice-Tay merges a fix for its memory growth
points: VI-BR-PORT's row is corrected. Its main branch took a new tree at 11:57 UTC whose README replaces its base and its figures, and this page's check of 12:22 UTC missed the change. The README (12:36 UTC) now reports about 12 frames a second in the playable prison section on an RTX 4060 Ti with 8 GB, on the smaller console's profile at 1080p, and about 5.6 on the larger profile. It says it is not playable yet and aims at 15 or more with a sharp picture.

By the rule that moves it from 10th to 3rd, 1 step short of the playable bar, behind klbf-lab and Vice-Tay; VIctory-7900XTX and Kelvaroq move down a place. The place rests on one figure for one scene on its new base and on the hour-long sessions it reported on its earlier base, which its README no longer gives and which stay in its stability lane, marked as such, until it reports a session on the new base. Nobody else has confirmed either.

Vice-Tay merged a fix at 12:32 UTC for the memory growth it blames for its slowdown: its notes say records of views were being kept for the whole run, 16.7 GB of them after 70 minutes. It has published no measured session since, so its lanes are unchanged and it stays 2nd.

VIctory-RDNA, on the watch list, now reports a median of 15.75 frames a second across the heavy-rendering samples of a capture of 13 minutes 37 seconds on a Radeon RX 7900 XT at 4K output, and says a full-session average and continuous time under player control are unverified. The estimate is unchanged.

updates.title: Estimate put back to early on Friday at a routine review; press relays claims of 25 to 30 frames a second, none with a session length
points: The estimate moves a quarter of a day later, to early on Friday 27 November, UTC, with about 4 in 10 by the end of Thursday. No published mark called for it: this is a routine review. The longest documented sessions sit at 13 to 14 frames a second, the fastest build slows as a session goes on, and no project has documented half an hour above 14 since the last revision. The new marks are in the revision note.

Press reports of 26 November, in TechRadar, Wccftech, GameGPU and VGTimes, relay posts and videos that claim 25 to 30 frames a second in the first boat mission for builds of the code PortWatch lists as CGBJ. GameGPU describes a group's demonstration at an average of 27 on an RTX 5070 Ti, read from an on-screen counter on open water. None gives a session length, the outlets call the claims unverified, and no row or lane changes. VGTimes also reports that a packaged build is circulating: this page links to no build, and downloads offered as GTA VI for PC have carried malware.

VIctory-7900XTX's README (11:48 UTC) reports a city street at about 22 frames a second on its Radeon RX 7900 XTX on the smaller console's profile with four renderer patches on, against 13 to 17 before them. The patches are off by default while they are tested, so its lane still reads 13 to 17 and it stays 3rd.

CBL VIctory, now read from its new default branch at its maintainer's request, reports a session of 65 minutes 46 seconds on an RTX 5080 at 4K output, through the boat sequence into the open world, closed by hand with no crash logged and with stretches measured at 4.3 to 11.4 frames a second. It moves from 17th to 9th, 2 steps short of the playable bar.

updates.title: Victory-United reports the player in control and moves to stage 6; VKarameloVI's repository stops answering
points: Victory-United's README (11:36 UTC) now reports the player in control: one session played by hand for 34.7 minutes in the first playable room on an RTX 3080 Ti, at half render scale on the smaller console's profile, at a median of 8.5 frames a second by its own log, closed normally with no crash. It calls control the player's own observation, not something its log measures, and claims nothing for this build's picture or for anywhere beyond that room.

It moves from stage 5 to stage 6 and is 8th of the 30 in-game rows, 2 steps short of the playable bar: speed from that session's median, stability from its 34 minutes, picture from what its README reported for an earlier build. The build merges VIctory-7900XTX's work into its tree, and nobody else has confirmed its figures.

The repository of VKarameloVI, a watch-list set-up of VIctory-NVIDIA's code on a second machine, stopped answering between 11:22 and 11:44 UTC: missing, private or removed, with no published takedown notice naming it and the reason not known. VIctory-NVIDIA's own repository still answers.
The first seven places and the estimate are unchanged. The estimate is next reviewed in the check after 12:00 UTC.

updates.title: Outside runs of CGBJ's code: 2.7 frames a second on its own settings, about 20 with one changed; victory-fork says the card is now its limit
points: A VIctory contributor's notes of this morning report runs of the code PortWatch lists as CGBJ on an RTX 3080 with 10 GB: 2.7 frames a second on that code's own settings, and a median of 19.6 with one setting changed, with minor glitches, about 19,000 textures still waiting for room on the card and no scene or run length given. HybridGt had measured the same 2.7 on an RTX 4070 Ti with 12 GB. Both are third-party runs that nobody has verified, and neither changes a lane.

The notes put the slow figure down to a memory cap that code applies on cards of 12 GB or less. PortWatch's entry still gives 25 on an NVIDIA card with 16 GB, and the repository still does not answer.

victory-fork's README (11:18 UTC) says its limit at the first boat mission is now the graphics card: 84 to 128 milliseconds a frame there on an RTX 4070, against about 60 for the layer's own preparing work after two measured gains that are still off by default, because its translated shader programs run to about 2.4 times the console's instruction count. It gives no new frame rates.
The standings and the estimate are unchanged. The estimate is next reviewed after 12:00 UTC.

updates.title: Vice-Tay's own figure for its played session is 12.9 frames a second over 70 minutes; klbf-lab is first again
points: Vice-Tay's README (10:35 UTC) now gives its own figures for the session played by hand through a scripted gamepad on its RTX 4090, on the smaller console's profile: 70 minutes in the world that it says never crashed or hung, at a median of 12.9 frames a second, with a tenth of its samples over 20.1 and a tenth under 8.3, and the game's memory at 52.3 GB at most on a PC with 43 GB. Its own summary is that it plays, is not fast enough yet and slows down the longer it runs.

The row reads that figure in place of this page's arithmetic from the play log, which had put the first 56 minutes at 15.2. It stays 1 step short of the playable bar and is now 2nd. klbf-lab, whose README still reports 37 minutes so far at 14.0, is first again on the higher frame rate. That is the third change of first place in an hour, each by the rule, between two builds that are both short of the bar on speed alone.

Flamingo's README (10:18 UTC) now gives about 9 to 10 frames a second in the first mission's boat cutscene on an RTX 4070 on the smaller console's profile, with shade lit by a stand-in floor of light. A cutscene is not play, so its speed and stability still read its 24-minute session of 25 November; its picture moves up a step and it is 12th. vilocity's latest run is back to about 11 after it took back a change that blacked out faces, and it stays 20th. five-star-recomp's status page says its city at night is now correctly exposed, at about 390 milliseconds a frame.

PortWatch's automatic check now records the repository it lists for CGBJ as not found, while its entry still gives 25 frames a second, and its board is led by a private build whose figures are self-reported, which this page does not list. VIctory-RDNA, a fork of VIctory-7900XTX that a reader asked about, joins the watch list. The estimate is unchanged.

updates.title: Vice-Tay logs 56 minutes of play, from about 20 frames a second down to 10, and takes first place; the estimate holds
points: Vice-Tay's play log (10:06 UTC) records a session on the smaller console's profile on its RTX 4090, played by hand through a scripted gamepad: 56 minutes without a crash through the opening, a boat mission, a camp and several fights, with deaths, retries, menus and the map all working. It is the longest played session at these speeds that any project has documented.

It also slows as it runs. The log's medians by the minute fall from about 20 frames a second in the opening rooms to 16 to 19 on the water, 12 to 16 in the camp and 8 to 13 in the last quarter of an hour, as the game's memory grows from 33 to 47.8 GB, past the 43.4 GB the PC has; the log calls that the likely cause, still to be shown. This page's arithmetic puts the session at 15.2 on average, and the project gives no figure of its own for the whole session.

The row now reads that session and is 1 step short of the playable bar, first ahead of klbf-lab, now 2nd with 37 minutes so far at 14.0, on the higher frame rate. The estimate is unchanged after the second reading: the length the bar asks for is there, 20 is not, and the only measured 20 is 10 automated minutes in the opening rooms. The mark for moving later at 12:00 UTC no longer applies, because sessions of 10 minutes or more averaging 15 or more have now been reported with their lengths.

Two forks on the watch list have looked at the code PortWatch lists as CGBJ. HybridGt reports building it as published and measuring a median of 2.7 frames a second on an RTX 4070 Ti with 32 GB of memory, and VIctory-forkAMD's notes say that code's own documents give 13 to 22 on a Radeon RX 7900 XTX with 40 to 46 GB of memory in use and about 16 to 18 on an RTX 5090. Both are third-party readings that nobody has verified, and PortWatch still relays 25. five-star-recomp's status page now says its city at night is on screen and lit.

updates.title: klbf-lab reports 37 minutes of play at 14.0 frames a second and takes first place; Vice-Tay measures 20.8 on the smaller profile
points: klbf-lab's README (09:38 UTC) reports a new test build, based on the Neptune edition of VIctory, in a session played with a controller on a Radeon RX 9070 XT: 37 minutes so far on foot and driving in the open world without a crash, at 14.0 frames a second on average, on the smaller console's profile with upscaling. Its measuring tool reads the layer's own frame lines and the measured settings use no frame generation. It is the best average published for a session of 20 minutes or more.

By the rule that orders stage 6 it is 1 step short of the playable bar and takes first place from VIctory-7900XTX, now 2nd, on the higher frame rate. The session was still running when read, the figures are one machine's own, and the row reads this build only: its earlier record of 77 minutes was at about 5.2 on its previous build.

Vice-Tay's README (09:32 UTC) adds a second automated 10-minute run on its RTX 4090, at a median of 20.8 frames a second on the smaller console's profile, the first median of 20 or more over a stated 10 minutes that this page has read in a project's own documents. That profile is not its default, so its row still reads 14.3 and it is 5th. Its play log follows a session played by hand on that profile, still running when read: 15 minutes logged at medians of 12.3 to 24.5 by the minute.

The estimate is unchanged at this check. None of these is the bar, which asks for 30 minutes at 20 or more in one session of play, and this page reads a new claim a second time before the estimate moves. Two forks that readers asked about, Neptune + GDeflate and VIctory-reloaded, join the watch list, and PortWatch now lists Kelvaroq as a tracked effort.

updates.title: Correction: Vice-Tay's 31-minute report is gone from its README; first place and the estimate go back
points: Correction to the update of 08:59 UTC. This page read Vice-Tay's README at 08:52 UTC and published at 09:00 UTC; by 08:55 UTC the README no longer carried the 31-minute gameplay test at an observed 20 to 25 frames a second, and it is not in the repository now.

In its place the README gives one measured session with nothing else running on the PC: 10 minutes in the world on an RTX 4090 at 4K on the larger console's profile, at a median of 14.3 frames a second. The row reads that: 2 steps short and 4th, and VIctory-7900XTX is first again.

The estimate goes back a quarter of a day, to around midnight UTC going into Friday 27 November, because the report that moved it is no longer made. From now on this page fetches a repository again just before publishing a change that rests on a new claim in it.
PortWatch's pinned note now says the code it lists as CGBJ was public and has since been taken down temporarily; it still gives 25 frames a second for it, and the repository still does not answer.

updates.title: Vice-Tay reports 31 minutes of play at an observed 20 to 25 fps and takes first place; not counted as playable
points: Vice-Tay's README (08:47 UTC) reports a gameplay test of 31 minutes 22 seconds on an RTX 4090, walking through the opening prison and using the in-game menus, ended by choice without a crash, with 20 to 25 frames a second observed. On its face that is the length and the rate this page's bar asks for.

This page does not count it as playable. The README gives a range its maintainer saw, not a measured average, and does not say on which profile, how the rate was read or whether every frame was rendered; an hour earlier it measured medians of about 13 on the same code at 4K with other work running on the PC, and those figures are still in it. Nobody else has confirmed the session.

Its lanes read both sets of figures: speed 12 to 25, a 31-minute session and a picture with faults. That is 1 step short of the playable bar, and first place changes hands: Vice-Tay leads VIctory-7900XTX and Kelvaroq on the tiebreak.

The estimate moves a quarter of a day earlier, to around the evening of Thursday 26 November, UTC, on the mark published at 05:41 UTC, met with that caveat. victory-fork's README now gives 8 to 9.5 frames a second at the first boat mission with a texture thread that is still off by default, and 10 to 14 in lighter views; it stays 7th.

updates.title: Vice-Tay rebuilds on CGBJ's code and reports 12 to 15 fps on an RTX 4090; the original repository still does not answer
points: Vice-Tay's README (08:25 UTC) says the fork now starts from the code PortWatch lists as CGBJ, and on it reports 12 to 15 frames a second indoors and in the yard on an RTX 4090 at 4K on the larger console's profile, with medians of about 13 over sessions of 6 to 8 minutes and longest sessions of 8 to 10 minutes without a crash. Its lanes now read the new base, and it moves to 4th from 7th.

The original repository still does not answer. Vice-Tay's README says its author took it down; this page has no statement from that author, GitHub has published no notice naming it and PortWatch still lists it as public. VIctory-7900XTX merged parts of the code at 08:05 UTC, so the work stays in public trees.

That gives a second reading of the same code: about 13 on an RTX 4090 at 4K in Vice-Tay's hands and 17 to 18 on an RTX 5090 in its own journal, against the 25 PortWatch relays. Nothing reports a session of 10 minutes or more at 20, so Playable stays at no and the estimate is held.

vilocity's latest test run shows a median of about 14 frames a second on its default profile, up from 11.5. five-star-recomp's status page says the city at night is on screen but washes out to white, with a world frame at about 540 milliseconds. News check: XDA has picked up PortWatch's 25 for CGBJ, no new notice names a project on this page, and there is no statement from Rockstar or Take-Two.

updates.title: CGBJ's repository stops answering within an hour of going public; the routine review holds the estimate
points: The repository PortWatch named at 07:23 UTC as the public code of CGBJ answered this page's read at 07:34 UTC and did not answer at 08:01 or 08:03 UTC, while other repositories did: it is missing, private or removed. GitHub has published no notice naming it and the reason is not known. The row keeps its place, 11th, without a link.

What was read while it was public stays as the row's reading: a fork of VIctory-7900XTX with six commits on top, medians of about 17 to 18 frames a second in the opening street on an RTX 5090 in its own journal, and no session of play. PortWatch still relays 25 and still lists the code as public.

Routine review of the estimate: held at around midnight UTC going into Friday 27 November. For moving earlier: the code was public for a time, PortWatch reversed the lowering that moved the estimate at 05:41 UTC, and VIctory-7900XTX reports about 19 in a city street with patches it is testing. Against: the journal's own figures are under 20, the repository is gone again, PortWatch's figure changed three times in four hours, and nobody reports a session of play with its length.

ScarlettPort reports 5.4 frames a second while walking and turning, up from about 4, and moves to 23rd from 28th. five-star-recomp says the world's lit image now reaches the screen, with surfaces still black. Native VIctory for macOS, a port that runs on Metal without Wine and gets past the start screen, joins the watch list.

updates.title: CGBJ's code is now public: PortWatch says 25 fps, its own journal 17 to 18; VIctory-7900XTX reports about 19 with new patches
points: PortWatch said at 07:23 UTC that the build it lists as CGBJ is now public as GPL-3.0 source, and put its figure back to an average of 25 frames a second in gameplay with 8 GB of system memory, after 25 and then 20 earlier today. Its entry still says independent reproduction is needed.

This page read the repository over git and now links it. It is a fork of VIctory-7900XTX with six commits of NVIDIA work on top. Its README gives no figures of its own, and its development journal records medians of 54 to 58 milliseconds a frame, about 17 to 18 frames a second, in the opening street on an RTX 5090 with 32 GB of memory around midnight UTC, in harness runs of about two minutes, with a sustained 20 still open then.

The row is now read from the project's own documents, as every public row is, with PortWatch's account relayed in its status: speed 17 to 18, a 2-minute run and a picture with open faults. That is 3 steps short and 11th, from 9th. Nothing reports a session of play with its length, so Playable stays at no and the estimate is held; with public code, anyone can now test the build.

VIctory-7900XTX rewrote its README at 07:19 UTC: its goal is a stable 30 frames a second or more without ray tracing, and a city street runs at 13 to 17 on its defaults or about 19 with two renderer patches that are off by default. It no longer lists the 41-minute session it reported on 25 November; this page keeps that reading and says so, and it stays first. News check: no new notice and no statement from Rockstar or Take-Two, and a second outlet, TalkEsport, reports the account of an email from Rockstar by the developer of the private build omonkey.

updates.title: Hourly check: no session lengths yet and no release of the private build; one more fork on the watch list
points: Neither PortWatch's entry for the private build CGBJ (20 frames a second, relayed) nor VIctory-NVIDIA's README (20 to 22 on average indoors) has added a session length, and the private build has not been released. Playable stays at no and the estimate is held.

Added to the watch list: ShakiraRED(dt), a performance fork of VIctory's code that AnyXboxX credits. On an RTX 4090 its README gives single samples from gameplay scenes, 18 to 20 frames a second in a lighter scene and 13.7 to 15 in a heavier one, with some draws dropped for missing pipelines and no session length. It has had no commits since 25 November.

VIctory-forkAMD's notes now report about 8.9 frames a second over a 15-minute run without a crash on a Radeon RX 7600, up from 6.2 to 6.4. VIniVIdiVIci withdrew the 7.3 it published at 05:35 UTC after finding a fault in one switch and gives 6.5 again, with switches that are off by default.

News check: the press has not picked up either report of 20 or more and still cites VIctory-7900XTX's 13 to 22 or older figures of 2 to 5. GitHub has published no new notice, and there is no statement from Rockstar or Take-Two since the build leaked beyond the notice against Leonida.

updates.title: PortWatch lowers its figure for the private build CGBJ to 20 fps; the estimate moves a quarter of a day later
points: PortWatch's stand-in editor changed its account of the private build CGBJ at 05:34 UTC: a stable 20 frames a second in gameplay, where it said an average of 25 at 03:58 UTC, with cutscenes at 30, on an NVIDIA card with 16 GB of video memory and 10 GB of system memory. It points to a video and says the build will be released soon, and still gives no session length and no word on whether every frame is rendered. The row reads 20 and stays 9th.

The estimate moves a quarter of a day later, to around midnight UTC going into Friday 27 November, as the mark published at 04:04 UTC said it would if PortWatch lowered its account. The promised release is not a mark; a session of 10 minutes or more averaging 20 or more, reported with its length, would bring the estimate forward again.

Correction: at 05:17 UTC this page read VIniVIdiVIci's speed lane from a median measured with switches that are off by default, 6.5 frames a second. Figures for a setup a project does not use by default do not count, so the lane reads 6.0 again. Its README now gives 7.3 with eleven such switches on, and its place, 18th, is unchanged.

OpenScarlett's README (05:20 UTC) reports a retail title it does not name through its intro video, menus and loading screens at 30 to 60 frames a second on a 4 GB GTX 1650 Ti, with live 3D gameplay as its next step. VIctory-NVIDIA and VIctory-7900XTX have published no new figures.

updates.title: No session lengths yet for the two fastest reports; small changes elsewhere
points: Neither VIctory-NVIDIA nor PortWatch's entry for the private build CGBJ has added a session length in the last hour, so both stay 3 steps short and Playable stays at no. VIctory-NVIDIA has not been updated since 03:41 UTC, and VIctory-7900XTX's README is unchanged.

VIniVIdiVIci's README (05:13 UTC) now gives a median of 6.5 frames a second in its first room with a set of switches that are off by default, and ScarlettPort's (05:02 UTC) about 4 while walking and turning on an RTX 3060, with its screen lighting passes fixed. Neither changes step or place.

On the watch list, XTP joins: a compatibility layer tested on a Radeon RX 6700 XT whose README says no title is usable yet. The hourly news check found the newest press pieces still putting builds at 2 to 5 frames a second or citing VIctory-7900XTX's 13 to 22, none reporting the 20 or more claimed since last night, no new notice and no statement from Rockstar or Take-Two.

updates.title: PortWatch stands by its CGBJ figures; Victory-United nearly doubles in its test room after merging VIctory-7900XTX's speed work
points: PortWatch's stand-in editor has added that the private build CGBJ averaged 25 frames a second on an NVIDIA card with 16 GB of video memory in a PC with 8 GB of system memory, and calls those figures "not a typo". No session length has been added, so its lanes and its place are unchanged.

Victory-United's README (04:41 UTC) reports a 15-minute run at a median of 9.3 frames a second in its test room after merging VIctory-7900XTX's speed work, against 5.0 before. The character still only stands in the room, so it stays at stage 5.

PortWatch now gives about 8 frames a second for the gameplay it saw on Belobug's fork, where it said about 4; that fork's README says 5 to 8. VIctory-NVIDIA and VIctory-7900XTX have published nothing new since the last check.

updates.title: A public fork, VIctory-NVIDIA, reports 20 to 22 frames a second indoors and joins the table; VItoriaBr moves to 3rd
points: VIctory-NVIDIA, a fork of VIctory-7900XTX made to run on NVIDIA cards, joins the table at stage 6. Its README has reported since 23:46 UTC on 25 November about 20 to 22 rendered frames a second on average indoors in the opening on an RTX 5070 with a Ryzen 7 9800X3D, and 24 to 31 in lighter places. This page found it only now, through a fork of it that PortWatch's scout listed.

The conditions matter: the smaller console's profile, the world drawn at 960 by 540 and upscaled, ray tracing mostly off, and its fastest settings, which leave some stretched bodies and miscoloured skin. One run each in the same PC measured 19.3 on the RTX 5070 and 14.9 on an RTX 5060 Ti, and a fork measured on an RTX 4060 Ti with a Ryzen 5 5600X, now on the watch list as VKarameloVI, reports 7 to 12. Its start script is set up for a driver feature that adds generated frames, and the figures here are its rendered frames.

It gives no session length, so it is on the speed step the bar asks for and 3 steps short on stability, in 11th place. It is the first public code to report an average of 20 or more in play, and with PortWatch's report on the private build CGBJ it is the second report of that kind today. The estimate, moved earlier at 04:04 UTC, is held: it already assumed a build near 20.

Also: VItoriaBr's README (04:09 UTC) now documents 4 to 6 frames a second on its current settings, where this page read 3.5 to 6 before, so the middle of its range reaches 5 and it moves from 10th to 3rd; its best open-world measurement of 22 comes from an experimental build that is not its default and is not counted. VIniVIdiVIci corrects its figures to a median of 6.0 in its first room, and five-star-recomp's lit world now shows a night sky at about one frame a second. The hourly news check found no press yet on PortWatch's CGBJ report, no new notice and no statement from Rockstar or Take-Two.

updates.title: PortWatch reports a private build, CGBJ, at 25 frames a second in gameplay; the estimate moves a quarter of a day earlier
points: PortWatch's update of 03:58 UTC, made by a stand-in editor, says PortWatch has now seen the private build CGBJ and reports an average of 25 frames a second in gameplay on an NVIDIA card, with interiors and cutscenes near 30 and a picture it rates close to the console with minor glitches. Until now it listed the build at about 4, unlit.

What the report does not give: a session length, the test machine beyond the card's maker, or whether every frame is rendered and none generated. The code is private, so nobody outside the group can test it, and PortWatch's own notes say its graphics degraded as speed improved before the rating was raised. This page relays it as unconfirmed.

CGBJ's speed lane now reads 25, the first row on the step the playable bar asks for. With no session length it is still 3 steps short and moves from 28th to 8th, and VIctory-7900XTX stays first. Playable stays at no: the bar asks for 30 minutes without a crash at 20 or more, reported.

The estimate moves a quarter of a day earlier, to around the evening of Thursday 26 November, UTC, with about 6 in 10 by the end of that day. The published mark asked for a session of 10 minutes or more averaging 20 with its length, which this report does not give, so the move rests on evidence the mark did not foresee and is undone if PortWatch withdraws or lowers the figure.

updates.title: VIctory-7900XTX pushes a night of speed work, with its README's figures unchanged
points: VIctory-7900XTX pushed code for the first time since it was published: merges of speed work made between 00:16 and 01:48 UTC, one of which its notes measure, standing in a street, at a mean of 88.8 milliseconds a frame against 100.5. Its README still gives 13 to 22 frames a second in most scenes and a longest session of 41 minutes, so its lanes are unchanged and it stays first.

Kelvaroq's README and its new release notes (03:24 UTC) restate its measurements without change: heavy frames at a mean of 7.6 frames a second in a 300-second run on an RTX 5080, and the outside tester's 36-minute session at 10 on average. Its lanes and its place are unchanged.

VIniVIdiVIci's README (03:22 UTC) measures about 6 frames a second in its first room over a scripted 280-second walk, against 4.9 before two changes to its pass over the descriptor heap, and says every session so far ran with a switch that is off by default. It stays on the second speed step, in 16th place.

Victory-United's README (03:30 UTC) now says moving the character is not confirmed: a run that held the move keys for about two minutes did not move it, so its figures are for standing in a room. It stays at stage 5.

updates.title: Two claims of faster private builds are not counted; BRVIctory-ka1qux reports its ray-traced street at about 3 frames a second
points: A reader reported on this page's issues that the private build PortWatch lists as NotNozy reached 20 frames a second in some sections of a live stream. PortWatch's own entry gives it no measured frame rate, crash record or test machine and marks it self-reported, so it is not on this page.

GameGPU relays a statement, posted on social media by a project it calls Portheon, that a closed build runs at 30 frames a second. The report gives no hardware, session length, footage, code or outside tester, and PortWatch does not list the build, so nothing is counted for it. This page still counts no build as playable, and its warning stands: any download offered as GTA VI for PC is fake.

BRVIctory-ka1qux's README (02:56 UTC) reports an open-world street at a median of 3.1 to 3.3 frames a second on a Radeon RX 7800 XT with the game's own ray-traced light on by default, the cost of each draw about a tenth lower than in its last build, and no crash in its last 50 runs of 4 to 25 minutes. Its place is unchanged.

Victory-United's README (02:55 UTC) records a paired 6-minute run in which 14 performance changes taken from other projects raised its first room from 4.0 to 5.0 frames a second. The hourly news check found no new notice and no statement from Rockstar or Take-Two beyond the Leonida notice.

updates.title: The speed lane now reads a session of play first; Kelvaroq passes AnyXboxX for 2nd
points: From this check a project's speed is read first from the average it reports over its newest session of play of 10 minutes or more, or its median where it gives no average. A project that reports no such session is still read from the middle of the frame rates it reports in play. Scripted or automated runs and scenes standing still do not count as play.

The reason is that low figures were not being read evenly. Since 00:11 UTC a rate given for a condition of play has counted as a row's low end, which was applied to AnyXboxX, VIctory-7900XTX and Flamingo but not to klbf-lab, whose README mentions dips to about 0.5 to 1 frames a second while a new area loads. A session average already includes such dips, and a sustained session is what the playable bar asks about.

Kelvaroq is now read from its unnamed tester's 36-minute session, 10 frames a second on average. That is the fourth speed step, so it is 1 step short of the bar and passes AnyXboxX for 2nd. klbf-lab reads 5.2 over its 77 minutes, Vice-Tay 7.0, Flamingo 8.6, Vertex 6.9 and ruff-lab 3.6, each on the same step and in the same place as before.

VIctory-7900XTX stays first. It gives no average for its 41-minute session and AnyXboxX's 13-minute runs are automated, so both are still read from their ranges, 5 to 23.8 and 1 to 17. No project's own figures changed in this check and the estimate is unchanged; victory-fork's run notes (02:17 to 02:30 UTC) record two more changes that cut copying or its submission thread's work without shortening the frame, and trace black surfaces in one area to textures the card had no room for.

updates.title: Flamingo's low figure is read like the leaders' and it falls to 13th; victory-fork measures a small gain
points: Flamingo's README has said since 25 November that its first scene falls to about 4 frames a second for a few seconds while turning, as textures stream in. That now counts as the low end of its speed lane, by the rule stated here at 00:11 UTC for AnyXboxX and VIctory-7900XTX: a rate a project gives for a stretch or a condition of play counts. The middle of its range goes from 10.9 to 9, which leaves it 3 steps short of the playable bar and takes it from 5th to 13th. Its own figures have not changed, and how every row's low figures and session averages are read is being reviewed.

victory-fork's README (02:15 UTC) measures one new change, a cache for buffer lookups, as saving about 14 milliseconds a frame on its test machine and another change as saving nothing. It says shadowed areas are still black and the graphics device is still lost 30 to 50 minutes into a session, with the PC's memory nearly full at two of the losses and no cause shown.

vilocity's README (02:01 UTC) says textures that were waiting for card memory now load, among them a print on one character's clothing and faces in the opening cutscenes, at the same 11 frames a second. Its runs still end at about 7 minutes.

Take-Two's notice against Leonida is now widely reported: TweakTown, Decrypt and heise are among those covering the 3,007 repositories GitHub removed, and KitGuru reports notices against repositories and chat servers without naming any. None of the reports read names another project as a target, GitHub has published no new notice, and neither Rockstar nor Take-Two has commented since the build leaked beyond that notice.

updates.title: Victory-United joins the table with a 35-minute scripted run; vilocity clears its slow launches
